slides.title: Which of the following medical asepsis actions should the nurse take to reduce and prevent the spread of microorganisms? Select all that apply.
text: Which of the following medical asepsis actions should the nurse take to reduce and prevent the spread of microorganisms? Select all that apply.
Applying a sterile gown and gloves.
Wearing clean gloves to prevent direct contact with blood or body fluids.

slides.title: Practicing hand hygiene. Yes, this is not a sterile procedure.
text: Practicing hand hygiene. Yes, this is not a sterile procedure.
Reapplying a sterile dressing. No, this is a sterile procedure.
Sterilizing contaminating items. No, this is a sterile procedure.
Applying a sterile gown and gloves. No, this is a sterile procedure.
Routinely cleaning the hospital environment. Yes, this is not a sterile procedure.
Wearing clean gloves to prevent direct contact with blood or body fluids. Yes, this is not a sterile procedure.
* Medical asepsis is clean technique and not sterile!!!

Use NON-Sterile gloves and hand hygiene

slides.title: Obligation To Report
The nurse is caring for a client with a decubitus ulcer (stage 4). The wound culture result shows MRSA in the wound bed. Which type of transmission-based precautions should the nurse institute?
text: The nurse is caring for a client with a decubitus ulcer (stage 4). The wound culture result shows MRSA in the wound bed. Which type of transmission-based precautions should the nurse institute?

slides.title: Standard. No, although they are used for all clients, standard precautions would not help decrease the spread of MRSA.
text: Standard. No, although they are used for all clients, standard precautions would not help decrease the spread of MRSA.
Droplet. No, MRSA in the nares would indicate droplet isolation.
Contact. Yes, MRSA in a wound indicates contact isolation.
Airborne. No, this isolation is indicated for very small molecules that linger for long periods in the air.
notes: If MRSA in nares its droplet

slides.title: Transmission Based Precautions Examples
The nurse is triaging clients involved in a mass causality disaster using the color-coded tagging system. Which clients should be tagged red? Select all that apply.
text: The nurse is triaging clients involved in a mass causality disaster using the color-coded tagging system. Which clients should be tagged red? Select all that apply.
Has full thickness burns over 30% of the body.

slides.title: Is deceased. No, this client would be in the black category.
text: Is deceased. No, this client would be in the black category.
Has chest pain. Yes, this client would be in the red category.
Has a leg sprain. No, this client would be in the green category.
Has a chest wound. Yes, this client would be in the red category.
Has multiple closed fractures. No, this client would be in the yellow category.
Has full thickness burns over 30% of the body. Yes, this client would be red since they have less then 65% burns on their body.

slides.title: The charge nurse observes a newly hired nurse caring for a client with a wrist restraint. Which of the following observations by the charge nurse requires follow up with the newly hired nurse?
text: The charge nurse observes a newly hired nurse caring for a client with a wrist restraint. Which of the following observations by the charge nurse requires follow up with the newly hired nurse?
A safety knot was used to secure the restraint.
The call light was placed within reach of the client.
The restraint was applied tightly around the client's wrist.
The clients record indicates that the restraint was released every 2 hours.

slides.title: A safety knot was used to secure the restraint. No, this is the correct type of knot to use.
text: A safety knot was used to secure the restraint. No, this is the correct type of knot to use.
The call light was placed within reach of the client. No, this is correct for safety.
The restraint was applied tightly around the client's wrist. Yes, the client's restraints should not be tight.
The clients record indicates that the restraint was released every 2 hours. No, this is the correct amount of time that restraints should be released for ROM.

slides.title: The nurse is discussing accident prevention with the family of an older client who is being discharged following hip surgery. Which of the following physical factors place the client at risk for injury in the home? Select all that apply.
text: The nurse is discussing accident prevention with the family of an older client who is being discharged following hip surgery. Which of the following physical factors place the client at risk for injury in the home? Select all that apply.
A night light in the bathroom.
A low thermostat setting on the water heater.
Common household objects such as a doormat or rug.

slides.title: A night light in the bathroom. No, this is safe.
text: A night light in the bathroom. No, this is safe.
Elevated toilet seat with armrests. No, this is safe.
Cooking equipment such as a stove. Yes, the client could burn themselves if they fall.
Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors. No, this is safe.
A low thermostat setting on the water heater. No, this is safe.
Common household objects such as a doormat or rug. Yes, the client could fall.

slides.title: Fall Prevention
text: Provide the client with nonskid footwear
Keep the floor free from clutter with a clear path to the bathroom (no scatter rugs, cords, and furniture)
Keep assistive devices nearby after validation of safe use by the client and family (glasses, walkers, transfer devices)
Educate the client and family/caregivers on identified risks and the plan of care
notes: Client Safety: Safety Precautions to Prevent falls

slides.title: Hazardous Waste
text: Any object in contact with body fluids, human body parts, placentas, etc.
dressings, swabs, blood bags, feces, urine, blood, sputum & lung secretions
If classification of a waste item is uncertain, as a precaution it should be placed into a
container used for hazardous health-care waste.

slides.title: Variances(Incident)
text: Any event or circumstance not consistent with the standard routine operations of the facility and its staff.
Significant medication errors and hazardous conditions
If you complete a variance, who do you need to notify?
(serious injury to or death of a client)

slides.title: The nurse is teaching a client with cardiomyopathy about safety measures when at home. Which of the following instructions is most important?
text: The nurse is teaching a client with cardiomyopathy about safety measures when at home. Which of the following instructions is most important?
Moving slowly from a sitting to a standing position.

slides.title: Reporting pain. No, this is important to educate but does not relate directly to safety.
text: Reporting pain. No, this is important to educate but does not relate directly to safety.
Taking a vasodilator. No, this is important to educate but does not relate directly to safety.
Avoid over the counter medications. No, this is important to educate but does not relate directly to safety.
Moving slowly from a sitting to a standing position. Yes, moving fast could result in orthostatic hypotension and the client would fall.

slides.title: The nurse is assigning clients to a LPN/LVN and UAP. Which clients should the nurse assign to the LPN/LVN? Select all that apply
text: The nurse is assigning clients to a LPN/LVN and UAP. Which clients should the nurse assign to the LPN/LVN? Select all that apply
A client requiring a dressing change to the foot.
A client requiring passive range of motion exercises twice daily.
A client requiring reinforcement of teaching about a diabetic diet.
A client requiring vital signs every 8 hours.

slides.title: A client needing frequent suctioning. Yes, this is under the LPN scope of practice.
text: A client needing frequent suctioning. Yes, this is under the LPN scope of practice.
A client requiring a dressing change to the foot. Yes, this is under the LPN scope of practice.
A client requiring passive range of motion exercises twice daily. No, this can be done by the UAP.
A client requiring reinforcement of teaching about a diabetic diet. Yes, this is under the LPN scope of practice.
A client requiring vital signs every 4 hours. No, this can be done by the UAP.

slides.title: Which of the following actions should the nurse take when caring for a client with accidental poisoning? Select all that apply.
text: Which of the following actions should the nurse take when caring for a client with accidental poisoning? Select all that apply.
Place the client in a supine position.
Induce vomiting if a household cleaner was ingested.
Assess for airway patency, breathing, and circulation.
Determine the type and amount of substance ingested.
Remove any visible materials from the nose and mouth.

slides.title: Save vomitus for laboratory analysis. Yes, this is correct.
text: Save vomitus for laboratory analysis. Yes, this is correct.
Place the client in a supine position. No, this could result in aspiration pneumonia.
Induce vomiting if a household cleaner was ingested. No, this would cause the esophagus to suffer burns twice.
Assess for airway patency, breathing, and circulation. Yes, this is correct.
Determine the type and amount of substance ingested. Yes, this is correct.
Remove any visible materials from the nose and mouth. Yes, this is correct.
